decisions.statement: Nothing here plans a rule to be taken away or turned off.
An address is folded to lower case on both sides before being compared.
A rule claims an address by a literal matcher on `to` and by nothing else.
A catch-all rule matches on `all` and so claims no address.
An address any rule claims is left alone, whatever that rule is named.
An address claimed only by a rule that is turned off is named rather than claimed twice.
An address a rule claims that no persona declares is named in the plan.
Only an address under the zone's own domain is planned for.
The destination copied is the one the rules named `persona-auto` forward to.
Where no rule carries that name, every rule that forwards is read instead.
More than one destination is refused rather than chosen between.
No rule forwarding anywhere is refused rather than filled in from elsewhere.
A rule is named for the address it routes and the address it forwards on to.
A plan taken over the rules its own last plan wrote plans nothing.

definition: the routing rules a zone is short of, worked out from the addresses the personas declare
